It's another day, which means we have another round of Europe's best teams ready to battle it out on the biggest stage.

Matchday 2 of the 2026-27 UEFA Champions League continues Wednesday, with nine more games across the continent and plenty of mouthwatering clashes on the schedule.

Among the standout fixtures, Manchester City welcome defending champions Paris Saint-Germain in a heavyweight showdown, Real Madrid travel to the Italian capital to face AS Roma, and Liverpool head to Austria to take on LASK in one of our early matches.

stories.headline: MLB changes ALCS Game 3 start time to 1 p.m. due to inclement Cleveland weather
stories.summary: The start time for Game 3 of the ALCS on Thursday was moved up five hours to 1 p.m. ET due to expected inclement weather.
stories.body:
CLEVELAND -- The start time for Game 3 of the American League Championship Series on Thursday was moved up five hours to 1 p.m. ET because of expected inclement weather.

Major League Baseball announced the changed scheduled time of the game, which was originally scheduled to start at 6 p.m. ET, on Wednesday.

The Tampa Bay Rays and Cleveland Guardians were off Wednesday after opening the series with two games at Tropicana Field, an enclosed ballpark not subject to the elements. Rain is in the forecast for northeast Ohio on Thursday night as the series transitions to Cleveland's open-air Progressive Field.

The series is tied at one game apiece after the Guardians took Game 1 on Monday and the Rays rebounded to win Game 2 on Tuesday. They are scheduled to play Games 3, 4 and 5 at Progressive Field over three consecutive days through Saturday.

"The change, which is based on forecasted rain on Thursday night in Cleveland, is being made proactively in order to remain on schedule in the ALCS," MLB said in a statement.

The teams would return to Tropicana Field to play Games 6 and 7, if necessary, after a scheduled off-day Sunday.

stories.headline: Ducks rookie dons No. 95, channels Lightning McQueen in NHL debut
stories.summary: After a draft night trip to Disneyland to meet Lightning McQueen, the "Cars" synergy came full circle for the Ducks rookie's NHL debut.
stories.body:
Roger McQueen made his NHL debut for the Anaheim Ducks on Tuesday night. He brought inevitable references to the Pixar classic "Cars" with him.

When McQueen was drafted 10th overall in 2025, the Ducks presented him with a No. 95 jersey -- a reference to the car number of Lightning McQueen, the Owen Wilson-voiced protagonist of the "Cars" movies. After he was selected, the McQueen family went to the 55th floor of The Ritz-Carlton in Los Angeles to board a helicopter and fly to Disneyland in nearby Anaheim, where Roger McQueen met Lightning McQueen.

McQueen got the call on Monday night that he would be elevated from the AHL to play for the Ducks.

"I thought he got better in camp as he went along. He was one of those guys that would be pushing for a job," said coach Joel Quenneville of the center. "Roger's got some upside in what could be a really nice career."

On Tuesday night, before the Ducks' home game against Calgary Flames, McQueen took his customary rookie lap to start warmups -- wearing No. 95 and sans helmet -- while the arena speakers blared "Real Gone" by Sheryl Crow. While not a staple of arena rock playlists, it was wholly appropriate here: "Real Gone" is the opening track from the "Cars" soundtrack album and was featured in the film.

McQueen played 11:26 in his NHL debut with no points and a shot on goal. It wasn't a memorable night for the Ducks as they lost to the moribund Flames 4-2 in front of a sellout crowd.

One game down, many more to go for McQueen. When he was drafted, Roger's father Scott McQueen said that the "Cars" connection intensifies the spotlight on the young center as he begins his career.

"I think everybody kind of wants to fly under the radar and you know, and just play," said Scott, via the CBC. "He wants to prove himself as a player and not so much, you know, as a Disney character."

stories.headline: Mikel Merino says Arsenal are 'ready' for Premier League, Champions League double
stories.summary: Mikel Merino insists Arsenal are ready to go one better than last season and complete a Premier League and Champions League double.
stories.body:
Mikel Merino insists Arsenal are ready to go one better than last season and complete a Premier League and Champions League double.

Off the back of taking their first league title in 22 years, the Gunners have started this season with nine victories from 10 matches.

Arsenal's sole blemish so far arrived in a shock 3-0 defeat at Brighton which leaves them three points behind Manchester City in the Premier League. Mikel Arteta's men saw off Lille on Tuesday night to make it two wins from two in the Champions League.

The European triumph marked Arsenal's 14th consecutive victory in the group stage of the competition. The Gunners missed out on Champions League glory last term following an agonising penalty shootout defeat to Paris St Germain.

"It is an absolutely unbelievable run," said Merino of Arsenal's winning streak which stands at almost two years. "We know that we're making history.

"At the same time, we know how difficult it is to win games, so we give a lot of value and credit to the team for what we're doing.

"The goal and objective is to win the Champions League, to win the Premier League, to win everything. That's what the manager wants. That's what the fans want. That's what we as players want, too."

- Eberechi Eze on Arsenal competition: 'If you don't want to play you're not in the right place'

- Arsenal showed strength in depth in Lille win, but Gyökeres is a concern

And pressed as to whether he believes Arsenal are in a position to do that this season, the Spain international replied: "Absolutely. This is our mentality and the aim.

"We were so, so close last season. That proved to us that we are ready for it. Now it's about details. It's about being present and ready in the right moments, and of course we believe that."

Arsenal will bid to extend their winning run in the group phase to 15 when they travel to Germany to face Bayern Munich next week.

Before then, the Premier League champions will take on Nottingham Forest at the City Ground with midfielder Martín Zubimendi likely to be back in contention after he suffered an ankle injury in a training session following Arsenal's win against Leeds last weekend.

Piero Hincapié also suffered an ankle issue during the post-win training session at the Emirates Stadium.

"Zubi is much, much better," said Arteta. "Piero is improving, but it looks more significant. I think it will be a matter of weeks [before he is available], but we don't know exactly how many."

stories.headline: First-round Phantom Draft: An early look at who goes where, when bids will come
stories.summary: The AFL trade period is over and attention turns to the draft. So who goes where? When will bids land? Here's Jasper Chellappah's early, first-round Phantom Draft.
stories.body:
It's finally draft season.

Changes to draft points and matching bids make for complications on the four club-tied prospects in this Phantom Draft, but they also shorten the first round to 18 selections.

It's a hotly-contested race to be the first overall pick in the open draft. Midfielder Ethan Drever and goalkicker Arki Butler have inside track to be that choice for Essendon, but the decision is still to be narrowed down with Heath Mellody, Harry Van Hattum, and Gus Teixeira all making strong cases.

Bidding changes mean clubs may only match with two selections, and a 20% points loading is given to the Brisbane Lions for making the Grand Final whereas Port Adelaide and GWS receive a 10% discount for missing finals.

It means picks are absorbed within the first round to effectively shorten night one of the AFL Draft.

Recruiters love the depth of the crop that has emerged this year, but a real evenness in talent from 15 through 30 will make for volatile slides and rises come November.

Exactly five weeks out from the 2026 AFL Draft, this is ESPN's first-round Phantom Draft.

1. BID - Port Adelaide: Dougie Cochrane

Port Adelaide/South Australia

FWD/MID/DEF, 195cm

Essendon has all but guaranteed Port Adelaide it will be bidding on Cochrane first overall. He's worth the hype; a roaming key forward with midfield ambitions that played the final month of an injury-plagued top-age campaign behind the ball as a designated kicker. Cochrane has been the nominal first choice in this draft for 24 months and Port Adelaide will have no issue matching, and they've left the door open for clubs to come calling for picks seven and 12 in the lead-up to draft night.

Picks used: 7 and 12

2. Essendon: Ethan Drever

GWV Rebels/Vic Country

MID, 188cm

It's still far from a guarantee that Essendon opt for Drever but there's growing buzz around the powerful midfielder. An injury-free season set him up to dominate for club and state alike, with the Ballarat local producing gaudy numbers for the Rebels and Vic Country. He runs hard both ways, uses his legs to drive out of contest and has a penchant for kicking long-running goals. Similarly to 2016 when they selected skipper Andrew McGrath, the Dons don't have a clear no. 1 in the open pool.

In the mix: Arki Butler, Heath Mellody

3. Richmond: Arki Butler

Sandringham Dragons/Vic Metro

MID/FWD, 182cm

Richmond's decision here will be highly dependent on their intel into West Coast and Melbourne after them. Butler presents as the best on the board and most unlikely to be available at their next selection. He's a match-winner inside forward 50 with aerial strength and tricks at ground level, kicking goals in bunches and pinch-hitting with power through the middle. With a host of tall forwards and midfielders drafted in recent years, Butler fits nicely amongst the young Tigers nucleus but real interest in Harry Van Hattum could see them flip this order.

In the mix: Harry Van Hattum, Ethan Drever

4. BID - Carlton: Cody Walker

Carlton VFL/Vic Country

MID, 184cm

The Blues are banking on a Walker bid arriving after pick two. Picks 13 and 18 (which become 12 and 17 after a Cochrane bid) is enough to match a bid from three onwards with a minor points deficit. If Essendon surprises by reading out Walker's name in the first two the Blues must have contingencies in place so the son-of-a-gun doesn't slip through. Walker is worthy of a bid at two - he plays at breakneck speed with elite acceleration and evasiveness through the midfield, impressing week in, week out for Carlton's VFL side.

The son of Andrew opted to nominate the Blues over academy club Richmond this year which may dissuade the Tigers from making a bid, but this is close to the end of Walker's draft range and West Coast already has history bidding on Blues father-sons.

Picks used: 12 and 17

5. West Coast: Heath Mellody

Claremont/Western Australia

MID/DEF, 184cm

The hometown kid enjoyed the strongest finish to 2026 of any prospect. Mellody claimed the Larke Medal at the national championships, made his WAFL debut and was one of Claremont's best performers up to the grand final. His name sits comfortably amongst the best in the class with his work rate, clean hands and class by foot making him the perfect complement to Harley Reid and Willem Duursma.

In the mix: Arki Butler, Gus Teixeira

6. Melbourne (via Port Adelaide): Mitch Harris

Woodville-West Torrens/South Australia

DEF, 195cm

Melbourne made a deal to move up two spots in the draft, effectively jumping North's selection at the time. That pick now lands with Sydney but it shouldn't impact who the Dees had in mind. Harris is the bolter this year, rising from a likely second round prospect at the start of the season to the consensus best key defender in the pool. He locks down, intercepts and has shown flashes up forward, plus impressed in SANFL finals to finish the season against mature bodies. The Swans will have interest in Harris given their shallow key defensive stocks, but the Dees will kick off his draft range at this point.

In the mix: Harry Van Hattum, Heath Mellody

7. Richmond (via Port Adelaide): Harry Van Hattum

Northern Knights/Vic Metro

RUC/FWD, 205cm

Richmond would be thrilled to see Van Hattum get through to the pick they brought in via Port Adelaide. The big ruck trained with the club over pre-season and he ripped games apart at various stages of 2026. Van Hattum plays with a physical edge, follows up as an extra midfielder and uses the ball beautifully off his favoured right boot. He looms as the perfect replacement for skipper Toby Nankervis, so much so that Van Hattum could even be snapped up by the Tigers with their first selection before Melbourne gets a look in.

In the mix: Gus Teixeira, Mitch Harris

8. BID - GWS: Ethan Matthews

GWS made an early bid on Harry Kyle last year and Sydney can return the favour here. Trading into pick six via the Blakey deal puts the Swans firmly in the range of Matthews, an excellent midfield prospect that racks up the ball and uses it with composure off his left foot. GWS would be matching with pick 11 at this stage, and could look to trade points into future years on the night to maximise their draft hand while still landing their academy gun. Matthews is clearly the best Giants Academy prospect since Tom Green in 2019.

Picks used: 11 and 19

9. Sydney (via North Melbourne): Gus Teixeira

Sandringham Dragons/Vic Metro

MID, 181cm

If the top key defender is off the board the Swans will have an eye on the best available talent, having not drafted a top-10 talent since Logan McDonald and Braeden Campbell in 2020. Teixeira is the highly rated prospect that slides in this phantom, but could easily be snapped up by the Dees or Tigers prior. Playing with powerful drive in the forward half, Teixeira's impact with ball in hand has been a standout all season. He'll start his career as a general forward but there's little doubt amongst recruiters that Teixeira will soon be a midfielder at the next level.

In the mix: Mitch Harris, Tyson Bradley

10. Gold Coast (FA compensation): Sam Gayfer

Northern Knights/Vic Metro

FWD, 194cm

Gayfer is deserving of a top 10 pick this year and the Suns come into this selection through Ben King's departure. Even while bringing in Aidan Schubert their key forward stocks are thin and Gayfer is the competitive beast that Damien Hardwick covets. He crashes packs, pressures at ground level and can jump on heads to take massive marks. The Suns swooping here would be a blow for the Saints and Pies who are keen on the athletic tall.

In the mix: Tyson Bradley, Clancy Snell

11. BID - Brisbane: Caylen Murray

Lions Academy/Allies

DEF/MID, 183cm

The Keidean Coleman trade to Essendon at the death gives Brisbane three picks in the second round that will need to be consolidated to match a bid at this stage. The academy star has some similarities to Coleman in his precise ball use off halfback. He generates run and is safe with ball in hand, making the right decisions and creating space for himself and others. Murray appeals as a replacement for Dayne Zorko and could play significant football in 2027, with the Saints on the lookout for a ball user of his quality.

12. St Kilda: Wil Malady

Gippsland Power/Vic Country

FWD, 190cm

The Saints would love to see Gayfer here as a key forward option, but have a nice group of talls to pick from. Malady is the wildcard play, with excellent athleticism including a big leap and sensational agility at his size. He works himself into the ground as a link between the forwards and midfielders, but can also play deep as a dangerous aerial target.

In the mix: Sam Gayfer, Lochie Burrows

13. Collingwood: Tyson Bradley

Sandringham Dragons/Vic Metro

DEF, 195cm

The Pies are in the market for a tall at either end of the ground and will get one at this spot. Bradley is ultra composed and a steady kick out of defence, twisting and turning out of trouble and relieving pressure for his side. He also competes well in the air against key forwards including successful matchups on Malady and Gayfer in finals contests. Clubs have loved his leadership and character qualities so he could land even higher than this mark. Collingwood will be eager to see if Gayfer gets through as the nephew of premiership defender Mick.

In the mix: Sam Gayfer, Clancy Snell, Wil Malady

14. Melbourne (via Port Adelaide): Leo Steed

Swan Districts/Western Australia

MID, 176cm

If the Dees go tall with Harris or Van Hattum first they can get their midfielder here. Steed is ultra professional, a two-way runner and brings his courage and toughness to every contest. Recruiters are confident the WA hard nut makes it as an on-baller at the next level and Melbourne is primed to add youth to that area of the ground.

In the mix: Toby Krasna, Jake Eime

15. Adelaide: Clancy Snell

Gippsland Power/Vic Country

DEF, 196cm

The Crows held onto Nick Murray but lost Jordon Butts and are thin down back. Snell gives them a high-upside swing at the best intercept defender in the class. He's an elite aerialist that backs himself to kickstart transition. They remain in need of some dash out of defence with local product Jake Eime's range beginning at this point too.

In the mix: Tyson Bradley, Jake Eime, Kodah Edwards

16. St Kilda (via Geelong): Lochie Burrows

Sandringham Dragons/Vic Metro

DEF/MID, 181cm

The Saints are keen on Burrows. A local Bentleigh product whose best trait may be his versatility, Burrows has been thrown around the ground and excelled everywhere. He can get his hands dirty as a contested midfielder, lock down and offer dash out of defence and worked hard on his forward craft over pre-season with an eye to a role off half forward. If the Saints sniff out interest in Burrows around this mark they could even snap up the high-character talent with their first selection.

In the mix: Leo Steed, Jackson Phillips, Jake Eime

17. Essendon (via Hawthorn): George Dimer

Sandringham Dragons/Vic Metro

FWD, 173cm

Dimer earns big plaudits from clubs for his character and selfless nature. As a small forward he has the speed to separate and the nous to sniff out the goals but also plays with a team-first attitude that sees him set up a lot of scores. He played midfield in his juniors and brings his ball-winning to the forward half. Small forward is a huge area of need for the Dons but there will also be a host of clubs keen on Dimer from this stage on.

In the mix: Clancy Snell, Jack Pickett, Toby Krasna

18. Fremantle: Jake Soutar

East Perth

DEF, 190cm

The Dockers are entrenched in their premiership window and Soutar would have played significant football at a lot of clubs towards the end of 2026. The 20-year-old was East Perth's fairest and best after a breakout season in the WAFL, intercepting and creating off halfback including a big finals campaign. He's a good size to play on various forwards and has the body to compete for Luke Ryan's role straight away. A mature-ager is a bold selection in the first round but Soutar is a win-now pick in a role Fremantle needs to address.

In the mix: Leo Steed, Toby Krasna

stories.headline: When can Kimi Antonelli win the F1 title? Earliest date, points needed and remaining races
stories.summary: Kimi Antonelli took another big step towards his first world title after outscoring his two closest championship rivals, George Russell and Lewis Hamilton, at the Singapore Grand Prix.
stories.body:
Kimi Antonelli took another big step towards his first world title after outscoring his two closest championship rivals, George Russell and Lewis Hamilton, at the Singapore Grand Prix.

The 20-year-old, who has the potential to set a new record for the youngest Formula 1 champion this year, now leads Mercedes teammate Russell by 102 points in the standings with a maximum of 150 points still up for grabs.

The substantial lead means he could be crowned champion as early as Oct. 24 at the U.S. Grand Prix in Austin, but the maths around that calculation are slightly complicated by question marks over the final two races of the season. The grands prix in Qatar and Abu Dhabi are currently scheduled to go ahead on Nov. 29 and Dec. 6, but escalations in the war between the United States and Iran have the potential to force the cancellation of both rounds.

F1 has put a contingency plan in place to hold a single round at Imola if Qatar and Abu Dhabi are cancelled, but doing so would cut the championship short by one round and mean only 125 points are available to any single driver before the end of the year. Such a scenario would change the maths around the championship fight, making it easier for Antonelli to be crowned champion in Austin.

- 'Chucky' Verstappen is back. Luckily for Antonelli and Mercedes, it's too late

- Max Verstappen takes back-to-back wins with dominant drive at Singapore GP

- Lewis Hamilton calls Singapore GP strategy 'painful lesson' after Ferrari apology

Alongside Russell and Hamilton, Max Verstappen, Charles Leclerc and Lando Norris are still mathematically in contention for this year's championship, although the incredibly slim hopes of Leclerc and Norris would be snuffed out entirely by the cancellation of the races in the Middle East.

What does Antonelli need to do to be crowned champion in Austin?
Assuming the final two races go ahead as planned, Antonelli's chances of clinching the title in Austin remain relatively slim. The Mercedes driver would need to win in Texas, with his teammate Russell finishing ninth or lower and Hamilton finishing fifth or lower.

Such a scenario would put Antonelli 125 points ahead of Russell with 125 points remaining, but even if Antonelli failed to score another point and Russell won all the remaining rounds after Austin, Antonelli would still be crowned champion on countback of race victories (by that stage Antonelli would be on nine and Russell on three with five races remaining).

If the championship is shortened by the season ending in Imola rather than Abu Dhabi, Antonelli would only need to leave Austin with a lead of 100 points over his rivals.

Such a scenario would result in the following permutations:

If Antonelli wins in Austin he would be crowned champion regardless of where the others finish.
If Antonelli finishes second, he would be crowned champion if Russell doesn't win the race.
If Antonelli finishes third, he would be crowned champion if Russell finishes off the podium.
If Antonelli finishes fourth, he would be crowned champion if Russell finishes behind him and Hamilton does not win the race.
If Antonelli finishes fifth, he would be crowned champion if Russell finishes fourth or lower and Hamilton does not win the race.
If Antonelli finishes sixth, he would be crowned champion if Russell finishes fifth or lower and Hamilton does not win the race.
If Antonelli finishes seventh, he would be crowned champion if Russell finishes sixth or lower and Hamilton does not finish in the top two.
If Antonelli finishes eighth, he would be crowned champion if Russell finishes seventh or lower, Hamilton does not finish in the top two and Verstappen does not win the race.
If Antonelli finishes ninth, he would be crowned champion if Russell finishes eighth or lower, Hamilton does not finish in the top three and Verstappen does not win the race.
If Antonelli finishes tenth, he would be crowned champion if Russell finishes ninth or lower, Hamilton does not finish in the top three and Verstappen does not win the race.
If Antonelli fails to score, he would be crowned champion if Russell finishes ninth or lower, Hamilton finishes fifth or lower and Verstappen does not win the race.

What's the minimum Antonelli needs to do be crowned champion?
Another way to look at the championship is the minimum amount of points Antonelli needs to score over the remaining rounds to secure the title regardless of what other drivers achieve. Assuming Qatar and Abu Dhabi go ahead, he needs 49 points over the remaining rounds, which could be achieved with as little as five sixth place finishes and one fifth place finish over the rest of the season.

If only five races remain, Antonelli would need just 24 points to secure the title, which would be attainable with two seventh place finishes and three eighth place finishes at the remaining rounds.

stories.headline: The UFC's flyweights are hot again - is Lone'er Kavanagh the next star?
stories.summary: Could a breakout win at UFC 333 propel Britain's Lone'er Kavanagh into the flyweight title picture?
stories.body:
The fighting life of a UFC flyweight was once an unenvied one.

Constant uncertainty over the future of the division, a lack of big pay-per-view interest and an unfortunate routine of far too many fighters getting cut for the weight class to sustain itself were just some of the problems that characterised the modern era. UFC president Dana White put it in simple terms, saying after Demetrious Johnson's UFC exit in 2018 that "people didn't care" about the flyweights. Even Olympic gold medalist and former two-division champion Henry Cejudo struggled to see how the flyweight division would continue as a part of the UFC, with his own brash persona and entertaining title defences pivotal to maintaining awareness of the division.

Much has changed since the days of Cejudo though, and the flyweights now have a genuine claim to being one of the most exciting divisions in the whole of the UFC. And one man at the forefront of that charge is another promising fighting talent from across the Atlantic, with England's Lone'er Kavanagh enjoying a rise like few others this past year.

He accepted a short-notice fight against ex-champion Brandon Moreno in the lion's den of Mexico City in March and produced one of the most stunning UFC upsets in recent memory, taking the unanimous decision win in front of a hostile crowd. Kavanagh was unranked before that fight and despite more recently losing to Brandon Royval at UFC 329, he remains just a win away from breaking into the flyweight title conversation. Taking on Royval on the night of Conor McGregor's return in Las Vegas in July, Kavanagh was submitted but earned the fight of the night on one of the promotion's most-watched recent cards in a back-and-forth slugfest. The 27-year-old's exciting style and high ceiling was on show that evening and will be again when he faces Ramazonbek Temirov on what is remarkably just his second high-profile numbered event at UFC 333 on Oct. 24.

"Thinking back to certain moments [in Mexico City], it was like a rollercoaster, it was a sick opportunity and I'm glad I did it and my team backed me to do it," Kavanagh tells ESPN.

"[Royval was] another step on the journey, losing is never fun, no matter what stage you're at whether you're at the top or at any point of your career but unfortunately sometimes you have to learn like that -- learning on the go, that's what we're doing right now.

"I believe I've got the best team around me so I truly believe with this team I can make it all the way to the top and that's the plan, that's the aim.

"I'm always trying to work on things from every fight. Unfortunately, you learn a lot more when you lose."

For Kavanagh, the lights have quickly turned brighter. Like many of his British counterparts in the UFC, he was made in Cage Warriors, the organisation that can take credit for the likes of McGregor, Paddy Pimblett and Tom Aspinall. From there, a first round knockout on Dana White's Contender Series saw the journey in the big time begin. His first professional defeat came in the UFC against the experienced Charles Johnson, but that was quickly forgotten with the Moreno heist that saw his stock in the game skyrocket. Kavanagh's front-footed, devious style stemming from his kickboxing roots has even earned him praise from one of the greatest to ever step in the octagon with a Jon Jones Facetime after that UFC Mexico win leaving him "starstruck."

"Your Muay Thai is beautiful, your kicks, they don't show at all. They have no telegraph. It's so nice," Jones said to Kavanagh.

It is a style that was born at London's Great Britain Top Team (GBTT), where alongside UFC veteran Nathaniel Wood and fellow prospect Shanelle Dyer, Kavanagh has honed his craft, going from a five-time K1 kickboxing champion to now potentially a statement win away from challenging for UFC gold under British MMA trailblazer Brad Pickett. And that too in a division where the competition is possibly as fierce as it has ever been. Royval, Tatsuro Tairo, Manuel Kape, Asu Almabayev and bona fide flyweight royalty Alexandre Pantoja make up the spine of a group of challengers that Kananagh finds himself a part of.

Joshua Van's UFC 331 title defence ended any doubts about his validity as champion, with a dominant win over Pantoja, and at just 24-years-old he looks set for a stint at the top -- where Kavanagh aspires to be. But first, No. 7 ranked, one below Kavanagh, and unbeaten in the UFC, the explosive Temirov is one of the toughest challenges the Englishman has faced in his career, and in a weight class as deep as the flyweights, back-to-back losses would see Kavanagh fall mercilessly down the pecking order -- the stakes are high at UFC 333.

"I think the flyweight division is the best division at the moment. It's forever changing," Kavanagh says. "There are so many young up and comers but there are also so many people that have been around for so long. So it's got a good mixture of everything and to be honest, just excited to be a part of it - it's sick being a flyweight at this time.

"I'm a very 'one fight at a time' kind of person, I'll always look at what's in front of me and then what's next but I think it would be an exciting fight either way, [Joshua] Van vs. Lon."

Born in London to an Irish father and Chinese mother, Kavanagh wears his heritage on his sleeve with his name Lone'er translating to "Little Dragon" in English. He credits his mum for pushing him into MMA, a decision that has since paid dividends.

Kavanagh is now set to be a part of a main card alongside two title fights at the Etihad Arena in Abu Dhabi. In his way, Uzbekistan's Temirov is coming in red hot on the back of a first-round finish against Steve Erceg, he last tasted defeat in an MMA bout seven years ago and has never been knocked out.

"I haven't seen all the fighters just fighting like me. Just striking punches, just making knockouts. But my punches will just kill them all," Temirov told the UFC.

The kickboxer is aware of the danger that Temirov carries but also the opportunity up for grabs.

"I think a win there puts me right back up there. He's a dangerous opponent. He's got some good wins under him, a lot of wins, but I think a win against him puts me right back up at the top. [I'm] always looking for a finish," Kavanagh said.

"His main weapons are his heavy hands, and that excites me. I love fights like that and I think it's a good fight for me. Hopefully [another fight of the night], I'm looking for more performances of the night."

As is now customary with Kavanagh's UFC bouts, his throwdown against the formidable Temirov is one not to be missed. With the top of the flyweight division so deep he will want to turn all the excitement surrounding him into consistency to earn a shot at Van's belt, that journey will take its latest step in a treacherous division.

And as Bruce Buffer introduces both fighters, perhaps there will be something for the UFC bosses and fans alike to take away before a single punch is even thrown. That all these years after Cejudo and Johnson have been and gone, the flyweights are box office property once again.

stories.headline: Dream's Gray has minor procedure on hand ahead of Finals opener
stories.summary: Allisha Gray, who has missed the Dream's past two playoff games because of a left hand injury, is still day-to-day heading into the WNBA Finals after undergoing a minor procedure.
stories.body:
Four-time All-Star Allisha Gray underwent a minor procedure on her left hand and is still considered day-to-day for the Atlanta Dream heading into the WNBA Finals, she said Tuesday.

"Progress is great," Gray told WSB-TV when asked at practice whether she'd play in Game 1. "As of right now just day-to-day, and you'll see."

Gray did not clarify whether she had surgery on her hand, and the team declined to say when the procedure occurred.

She was seen taking shots at practice Tuesday, a day before the team travels to the Bay Area for Saturday's Finals opener against No. 2 seed Golden State.

Gray, the top scorer for the No. 4 seed Dream, has missed the past two playoff games after injuring the hand in the first half of Game 1 in a semifinal series against the New York Liberty. She was listed as questionable heading into Game 3 last Friday against New York and went through warmups before being ruled out "in the interest of caution," according to coach Karl Smesko.

The Dream advanced to the Finals with a three-game sweep.

Gray, a 6-foot guard out of South Carolina, averaged 19.0 points, 3.5 rebounds, 2.6 assists and 1.4 steals this year while appearing in all 44 regular-season games. She was also the Dream's top scorer (22.0 points per game) during their first-round sweep of the No. 5 seed Washington Mystics.

The Dream and Valkyries will both be competing for their first WNBA championship.

stories.headline: Garber won't dish on exchange with Messi: 'Between me and Leo'
stories.summary: Don Garber has addressed his September confrontation with Lionel Messi, and the MLS commissioner said he admired the exchange.
stories.body:
Don Garber has addressed his confrontation with Lionel Messi following Inter Miami CF Campeones Cup victory over Cruz Azul in September, with the MLS commissioner saying he admired the exchange.

Following the Campeones Cup victory, Messi and Garber could be seen having a heated discussion before the Inter Miami captain went to celebrate the victory with the rest of his team and family members.

"You know, the best players in the world have passion," Garber said in an interview with Front Office Sports on Tuesday. "The legendary players have more than passion. Leo played on Saturday, scored a couple goals and assists coming out of an international window where he played for Argentina, 39 years old. He's leading our rush for Golden Boot. He's leading our MVP race.

"There are players throughout history, Muhammad Ali, Wayne Gretzky, Michael Jordan who play with a sense of intensity and passion that makes them unique and special, and makes him the GOAT of all GOATS. What is going on there is between me and Leo [Messi], it's not something I am going to talk about with you.

"But I admire it, I appreciate it and I think it's what makes Leo Messi the greatest player ever to play football. And I will say, [he's] the greatest athlete of all time."

Inter Miami beat Cruz Azul 2-0 in the Campeones Cup final with a goal from Messi in the 24th minute before he provided the assist to Casemiro for the second goal. Messi currently has 23 goals and 13 assists in MLS, leading the 2026 Golden Boot race and sitting in second place for most assists so far this regular season.

It's not the first time that Garber and Messi haven't seen eye to eye. In 2025, Garber made a joke about Messi not wanting to talk to him following the decision to suspend him and former teammate Jordi Alba for missing the 2025 MLS All-Star Game.

"I don't think he wants to talk to me," Garber said in 2025. "I didn't treat him like any other player in that decision. So, I probably won't be going to Miami any time soon or hanging out and doing any media work with Leo."

Garber later defended his decision to suspend the two players.

"If you don't do that, you're not gonna be able to lead," Garber said. "You're not gonna be able to command the respect of the ownership. The media is going to s--- on you no matter what. You guys will write a story 'how could you suspend Leo Messi?' after we suspended him, and before we suspended him say 'how could you not?'

"So, the media is irrelevant to that equation. They're gonna hate you all the time."

Garber and Messi later interacted at the 2025 MLS Cup, when the MLS commissioner presented the Inter Miami captain with the trophy. Inter Miami currently sits second place on the Eastern Conference table with 49 points from 28 games.

stories.headline: NRL: Spencer Leniu signs with Eels after early Roosters release
stories.summary: Spencer Leniu has signed a four-year deal with Parramatta just days after winning his fourth NRL premiership with the Sydney Roosters.
stories.body:
Spencer Leniu has signed a four-year deal with Parramatta just days after winning his fourth NRL premiership with the Sydney Roosters.

Leniu finished his three-year stint at the Tricolours on a high after a stellar performance in their 19-18 win over Newcastle to secure the 2026 trophy.

The NSW Origin representative added the Roosters' premiership ring to the three he won with Penrith from 2021-2023.

Leniu was granted a release from the final year of his Roosters contract, which will give the club some salary cap reprieve

The hard-hitting forward's Eels contract is reportedly worth more than the $850,000 per year he was making with Easts, where he spent much of his time coming off the bench.

He is expected to play a more active role in blue and gold, leading the line for the Eels' forward pack.

The westward move will see the former Panther reunite with good friend Jarome Luai, but first the pair will both suit up for Toa Samoa at the Rugby League World Cup.

Eels general manager of football Mark O'Neill shared his delight at signing one of the game's "premier enforcers".

"We're thrilled to have Spencer join the Parramatta Eels and become part of what we're building at this club," O'Neill said in a statement.

"He's one of the elite middle forwards in the game and has consistently performed on the biggest stages throughout his career.

The exit of Leniu adds to the exodus of stars from the Roosters premiership lineup.

Angus Crichton and Mark Nawaqanitawase are rugby-bound, Daly Cherry-Evans is joining Hull FC, while Daniel Tupou retired this week after his 307-game career.

Connor Watson, who missed the title decider due to concussion, has signed for a season with St George Illawarra Dragons.

Roosters coach Trent Robinson said Leniu had been a strong contributor during his time at the club.

"Spencer has brought a lot to our group over the last three years, both through the way he plays and the energy and personality he brings every day," Robinson said in a statement on Thursday.

"He brings an intensity and competitiveness to everything he does, and he challenges the people around him to be better.

"To see him finish his time here as a premiership winner is something he should be really proud of, and something we'll always share together."

With his departure announced at the Roosters' awards night on Wednesday, Leniu said he would leave the club on a high.

""I'm proud to have worn the Roosters jersey and I'll always have a lot of love and respect for the club, the boys and everyone who has supported me during my time here," said Leniu.

"Winning a premiership with this group and sharing that with the boys, our families and everyone at the club is something I'll carry with me for the rest of my life."

stories.headline: Lamine Yamal: Assist for Anthony Gordon in Barcelona win 'almost-rabona'
stories.summary: Lamine Yamal christened his dribble leading to Anthony Gordon's goal against Galatasaray an "almost-rabona" as Barcelona ran out 4-1 winners in the Champions League game.
stories.body:
Lamine Yamal christened his dribble leading to Anthony Gordon's goal against Galatasaray an "almost-rabona" as Barcelona ran out 4-1 winners in the Champions League game.

Yamal, 19, didn't score in the victory in Istanbul but produced a stunning second half display, setting up Fermín López with a pinpoint cross before creating for Gordon.

The teenager shaped to do a rabona, tricking the defender, only to knock the ball towards the byline instead. He benefitted from a small ricochet, but reacted quickly to drive inside before assisting the England international.

"I don't know what to call it, it was an almost-rabona dribble," Yamal told Movistar after the game as he watched a replay of the goal.

"It came off well to set up Gordon, that's the main thing, that it was effective at the end of the day."

In a separate interview with CBS, Yamal told former Barça forward Thierry Henry he is always looking for new ways to create space.

"Recently, I have noticed that a lot of opponents, whenever I reach the byline, go to ground, so I saw the opportunity, went for it and it came off," he added.

"I always try to faint to create space. If you can create a bit of space that way, it gives us [attackers] life. It was nice, but also effective, so I am very happy."

- Transfer rumors, news: Real Madrid, Barcelona chase Spurs defender Porro

In 10 appearances for Barça this season, Yamal has now scored eight goals and laid on nine assists.

Barça coach Hansi Flick credited him with "changing the game" against Galatasaray as the Spanish champions recovered from going behind to run out convincing winners.

"In the second half he was fantastic, how he dominated the game, the last pass ... It's unbelievable what he's doing," Flick said in the post game news conference.

The victory in Türkiye was Barça's 10th in a row at the start of the current campaign -- eight in LaLiga and two in the Champions League.

During that time, they have netted a remarkable 43 goals, with Yamal saying they are laying the foundations for potentially historic season.

"Always," he told CBS when asked if Barça believe a Treble -- winning LaLiga, the Champions League and the Copa del Rey -- is possible this season.

"We're Barcelona, we're the best team in the world."

That claim will be tested over the next week as Barça travel to third-placed Real Betis in LaLiga on Saturday, face Paris Saint-Germain in France in the Champions League next Tuesday and then host Real Madrid in the first Clásico of the season the following Sunday.

stories.headline: Who is this year's Mr. October? Tracking the playoff MVP for 2026
stories.summary: We go inside the numbers on the players doing the most to help their teams win.
stories.body:
Who is hero of the 2026 MLB playoffs?

To try to answer to that question, we're tabulating the cumulative win probability added figures for every player in the postseason. But we've added a twist: The deeper we get into the playoffs, the more weight the WPA carries. The division series counts double the wild-card round, then we'll double it again for the championship series and, finally, once again for the World Series.

This means that players who shine in the early rounds can still get on the leaderboard, but it's more difficult. Coming through when the championship leverage is at its highest is what becoming an October hero is all about.

Tuesday's hero: Freddy Peralta was on point in Game 2 of the ALCS, putting up six zeroes as the Rays evened the series. Peralta's ERA over two playoff outings so far is 0.84. His game score of 68 was the best of his eight career postseason starts and the six innings made it his longest outing yet. Pitchers continue to dominate the HeroAXE leaderboard and for good reason: Teams are averaging just 3.47 runs per game in the playoffs, the lowest figure since 1991.

Methodology
As mentioned above, each player's win probability added (WPA) is tracked on a per-game basis. Each round of the playoffs counts double that of the previous round. The tabulation is then converted to an AXE-style index in which 100 represents the average for all postseason players. The "Change" column looks in the changes in AXE numbers from the previous day for players who were in action. You can sort this column by clicking on it to see the day's heroes.

stories.headline: NHL Tonight: What to watch in Capitals-Canadiens, Stars-Avalanche
stories.summary: With just two contests on the NHL calendar Wednesday, here are game previews, betting lines, updated stat leaders and more.
stories.body:
After the hockey overload of Frozen Frenzy on Tuesday -- with all 32 teams in action -- Wednesday's schedule is a much lighter dessert, although both matchups are quite tantalizing.

The early game features the returning Eastern Conference finalist Canadiens against the Capitals, who hope to have a long playoff run in Alex Ovechkin's final NHL season. In the second game, two Western Conference juggernauts -- the Stars and the Avalanche -- hold a rematch just 24 hours after battling during the Frenzy.

Here's a look at the key stats and storylines in each contest, along with betting info and broadcast details:

Odds are provided by DraftKings and subject to change.

Montreal Canadiens at Washington Capitals

7:30 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | WSH -130, O/U: 6.5

After being anointed as the next big thing during the preseason, the Canadiens have stumbled out of the starting blocks, posting a 3-2-1 record. Likewise, the Capitals were declared the unofficial winners of the offseason given their many wise trade and free agency additions, yet they are a touch worse with a 3-3-0 mark. Which team might start a hot streak with a W in this one?

Dallas Stars at Colorado Avalanche

8:30 p.m. ET (TNT) | COL -148, O/U: 5.5

It's rare for two teams to play each other on back-to-back nights, and even rarer for two members of the NHL's top echelon to do so. After finishing first and third in the league during the 2025-26 regular season, the Avs and the Stars have not quite gotten out to that type of start this campaign, but both are expected to be right in the mix come playoff time. The Avs won 3-2 in Dallas on Tuesday -- including another fight for Nathan MacKinnon -- how does this game turn out?

Fifty-nine years ago today was the start of a new era in the NHL. In the 1967-68 season, the league doubled in size, adding the California Seals, Los Angeles Kings, Minnesota North Stars, Philadelphia Flyers, Pittsburgh Penguins and St. Louis Blues in the new West Division, with the Original Six franchises making up the East Division.

On Oct. 14, 1967, two of those new teams -- the Kings and the Flyers -- would meet for the their NHL debuts at California's Long Beach Arena. The Kings won 4-2, with Brian Kilrea scoring both the historic first goal in franchise history as well as an empty-netter to seal the deal.

Each team has gone on to win two Stanley Cups in the time since -- 1974 and 1975 for the Flyers, and 2012 and 2014 for the Kings -- but the franchises have never met in a postseason series.

stories.headline: Fulham's Arbeloa fined for ref comments after Man United draw
stories.summary: Fulham's Álvaro Arbeloa was fined $33,200 and given a warning for his comments after a match against Man United that questioned the integrity of the referee.
stories.body:
Fulham manager Álvaro Arbeloa was fined £25,000 ($33,200) and given a warning Wednesday for his comments after a Premier League match against Manchester United after he claimed officials would "not let Manchester United lose."

Arbeloa accepted a charge that he "acted in an improper manner" with his remarks made following the 1-1 draw between the teams at Fulham's Craven Cottage on Sept. 20.

"I think all fouls for them," the Spaniard said at the time in reference to United, which had lost to Manchester City the previous weekend because of a contentious goal.

"Every decision was for them," Arbeloa said. "And I knew, I knew after the game against Man City that they don't let Manchester United lose here."

According to its written reasons published Wednesday, the independent commission investigating the incident "felt that those words suggested, not only that there was bias on the part of the match officials throughout the game on repeated occasions, but also that there may even have been an element of pre-meditation by them and/or others to try to make up for an error in a different match."

Arbeloa is in his first season with Fulham after leaving Real Madrid.

stories.headline: AFL tracker: every player who moved in free agency and the trade period
stories.summary: The offseason is upon us which means AFL trades, free agency, and player movement is about to take off. Here's the latest news, whispers, and confirmed deals.
stories.body:
It's AFL player movement season, with trades and free agency set to dominate the month of October. So who is going where? Keep track with our player movement guide here.

When is the AFL trade and free agency window?
The 2026 AFL trade period commences on Monday, October 5 and closes in the evening of Wednesday, October 14.

The free agency window opens and closes a little earlier; it runs from Friday, October 2 until Friday, October 9.

Wednesday, Oct. 14
Deadline day
Demons pick up defensive depth with Hawk

Bodie Ryan was a late trade, with the 21-year-old traded from Hawthorn to Melboune in exchange for pick 107 -- a token pick in the end.

Ryan played five games for the Hawks in 2026 but couldn't break into the team ahead of the myriad other medium defenders on the list.

Pedlar makes cross-town switch to Power

It took until the very final minutes, but Luke Pedlar has made the cross-town switch to the Power from the Crows.

Port Adelaide got Pedlar and pick 34, with pick 32 and a 2027 fourth-rounder tied to Richmond going back to Adelaide.

Keidean Coleman gets from Lions to Dons

The deal sees defender Coleman and pick 25 in this year's draft going to Essendon for picks 21 and 27.

Goater traded from North to Hawthorn

Josh Goater, the 22nd pick at the 2021 national draft, has made the move to Hawthorn in exchange for a future third-round pick, tied to Port Adelaide.

Viney and Rivers get to West Coast

Two wantaway Dees have secured their passage west, with Melbourne striking a deal to send Trent Rivers and Jack Viney to the Eagles.

Melbourne gave up Viney, Rivers, and a 2028 second round pick in exchange for West Coast's pick 45, future seconds in 2027 and 2028, and a 2027 fourth round pick.

Will McLachlan becomes a Demon

It took until the final 15 minutes of the trade period, but McLachlan has made his way from Brisbane to the Demons in exchange for pick 45, with a swap of future second-rounders.

McLachlan was pick 6 in the 2024 mid-season draft and played seven games for the Lions.

Tuesday, Oct. 13
Blues land gun Giant

Lachie Whitfield's move to Carlton is official, with the 32-year-old joining the Blues on a three-year deal. Whitfield has played 278 games, and joins Toby Greene, Jesse Hogan, and Jake Stringer in departing the Giants.

Carlton receive picks 31 and 50 along with the veteran, with pick 25, pick 26, and a 2028 third-round pick going back the other way.

Former top-five pick on the move

Zane Duursma has got his wish, joining Melbourne along with pick 52. The Roos get pick 33 and 49 in return.

Blues ruck crosses to Collingwood

Flynn Riley has been traded to the Magpies after joining Carlton in the mid-season draft this year, making his AFL debut in Round 18.

A 2028 third-round pick goes the Blues' way.

Swans trade star defender to North Melbourne

The biggest name left on the AFL trade board has tumbled, with Sydney agreeing to move Nick Blakey to North Melbourne.

The Swans offloaded Blakey, draft pick No.52 and their 2028 second-round selection in exchange for a glut of picks.

The Kangaroos traded picks No.6 and No.47, a 2027 second-round pick, a 2028 first-round pick and a 2028 second-round pick to get the deal done.

Monday Oct. 12
Suns land Schubert, Butler from Hawks

The Suns have landed their offseason trade target in Aidan Schubert from Hawthorn, in a package also involving Sam Butler and some picks going both ways.

Gold Coast gained Schubert, Butler, Hawthorn's 2028 first-round pick, and Hawthorn's 2027 third-round pick, in exchange for Gold Coast's 2028 first-rounder, and second rounders in both 2027 and 2028.

Friday, Oct. 9
Butters is a Bulldog

Zak Butters is officially a Western Bulldog. Port Adelaide will not match the offer and accept pick No. 5 as compensation, having also earlier secured picks 6, 10, and two future-firsts in the five-club mega trade. The star free agent and three-time All-Australian, who played 156 games and kicked 73 goals for the Power after being drafted in 2019, has signed a nine-year deal with his boyhood club.

Hawks land spearhead King

After securing Zach Merrett earlier this week, Hawthorn have officially welcomed Ben King today after gold Coast elected not to match the offer for the restricted free agent. the Suns will receive a first round pick as compensation, which currently stands at pick No. 7.

Mega trade approved

The league approved a mega trade involving Port Adelaide, the Bulldogs, Melbourne, Hawthorn and Carlton, two players and scores of picks.

Under the five-team deal, the Bulldogs gave up picks No. 12 and No. 31 and a 2028 first-rounder to bring in Hawthorn's Finn Maginness, Carlton's Hudson O'Keeffe and later picks in this year's draft and future years.

Port parted with picks No. 4, 46 and 81 and six second-round or worse future selections to get back picks No. 6 and No. 10, Melbourne's 2027 first-rounder and the Dogs' 2028 first-rounder.

The Demons surrendered picks No.6, 10 and 87 and their 2027 first-rounder -- as well as two late future picks -- for picks No. 4, 12, 31 and 46.

Hawthorn (2027 third-rounder) and Carlton (2028 fourth-rounder) received late future picks for Maginness and O'Keeffe.

-- AAP

Flag Lion gets his wish

Brisbane has traded second-year Lion and 2025 premiership player Sam Marshall and pick No. 39 to St Kilda for a 2027 first-rounder.

Thursday, Oct. 8
Marshall lands at the Cats

St Kilda have pulled the trigger on a deal to send contracted ruckman Rowan Marshall to Geelong, as the Cats and other rival clubs circle Sydney star Nick Blakey.

Geelong traded pick No.14 in this year's draft for the disenchanted 30-year-old and a third-round selection in 2028 on Thursday afternoon.

New Zealand-born Marshall had requested a move to the Cats for a second straight year after St Kilda recruited Tom De Koning to become their first-choice ruckman.

-- AAP

Wednesday, Oct. 7
Dons defender gets traded to the Cats

After being denied a trade last year, Jordan Ridley got his wish for a fresh start after Essendon and Geelong agreed to a deal on Wednesday.

Geelong gave up utility Jack Bowes, a 2027 first-round pick and 2028 second-round pick to get the 27-year-old Ridley through the door.

Pick No. 60 and a 2028 fourth-round selection will come back to the Cats from the Bombers.

--AAP

Tuesday, Oct. 6
O'Driscoll makes the move over east

Fremantle have traded 24-year-old Nathan O'Driscoll to Richmond in exchange for pick 61 in this year's draft.

The winger played 17 games for the Dockers this season but wasn't selected for the Grand Final.

Monday, Oct. 5
TRADE PERIOD OPENS
Merrett finally becomes a Hawk

After attempting to join Hawthorn last year, Zach Merrett has finally been traded from Essendon to the Hawks.

Hawthorn have sent picks 15, 25 and a 2028 second-round pick in exchange for the 31-year-old.

Merrett leaves the Bombers a week after winning a record-equaling seventh Crichton Medal, three All-Australian blazers, and 274 games.

Pendlebury becomes a Sun

AFL games record holder Scott Pendlebury is officially a Sun after Gold Coast and Collingwood agreed on a trade for the 38-year-old veteran.

Pendlebury, a two-time premiership player, heads to the Suns in exchange for pick No. 65 in this year's draft.

"It's an exciting group here at the SUNS and the opportunity to bring a few different ideas and also learn from a great group of coaches and players is one I'm really looking forward to," Pendlebury told the Suns.

"This side is one I've watched from afar and really admired. I've got a bit of knowledge about the industry so I'm here to play my role and help this squad continue to develop."

Jesse Hogan traded from GWS to Collingwood

Out-of-favour Giants forward Jesse Hogan has made the switch to Collingwood in exchange for pick 75.

The 31-year-old won the Coleman Medal in 2024 but has been unable to recapture his best form at the Giants in the two years since.

Magpies list boss Justin Leppitsch said Hogan would be a valuable addition.

"On behalf of everyone at Collingwood, I'd like to warmly welcome Jesse to Collingwood. Jesse has established himself as one of the competition's premier key forwards and we're excited to see him bring his experience and talent to our club," he said.

"His aerial presence inside forward-50 and his consistency as a goal-kicker make him a genuine threat.

"Like Lachie (Neale), Jesse has a passion to teach the next generation and will make a great addition to our club."

Saturday, Oct. 3
Bulldogs seal free-agency signing of key defender

The Western Bulldogs have finally snagged the key defender they need, securing Adelaide backman Jordon Butts as an unrestricted free agent.

The Bulldogs are set for a bumper AFL trade period headlined by working through a deal for Port Adelaide superstar Zak Butters, ahead of a 2027 season where the club will have high expectations.

But after seeing off Carlton's advances to keep hold of defender Buku Khamis, the Bulldogs have filled a major area of need by adding 26-year-old Butts.

Adelaide will receive a second-round compensation selection, currently pick No.33, in this year's draft.

-- AAP

Friday, Oct. 2
FREE AGENCY OPEN
Three-peat Lion locks in Magpies move

Lachie Neale has sealed his high-profile switch to Collingwood, with Brisbane teasing the dual Brownlow medallist on his way out the door.

The AFL approved Neale signing a three-year deal with the Magpies on Friday afternoon, closing out the first day of free agency.

The 33-year-old ball-winner leaves as an unrestricted free agent after the Lions clinched a third straight flag with their stunning seven-point grand final victory over Fremantle.

-- AAP

Greene on his way to the Cats

Toby Greene will join Geelong as an unrestricted free agent on a three-year deal, re-partnering with former Giants teammate Jeremey Cameron.

The paperwork was lodged to the AFL on Friday morning.

The Giants receive band three compensation for Greene, which is currently pick No. 26 in the upcoming draft.

Greene departs the Giants with his name etched in the club's record books, sitting first in games played for the club with a tally of 282 games, as well as leading the club's all-time goalkicking tally with 450 majors.

Briggs now a Tiger

Richmond has landed GWS ruck Kieren Briggs as an unrestricted free agent.

Briggs' move to the Tigers was confirmed just hours after the free agency window opened on Friday.

Briggs played 88 games for GWS after joining the club as the No.34 pick in the 2018 draft.

Amartey officially joins the Blues

Free agency has opened with a bang, with out-of-favour key forward Joel Amartey committing to Carlton.

Details are still to come on the length of contract, and Sydney's compensation.

Hawthorn father-son recommits despite interest

Calsher Dear has made a shock decision to re-sign with the Hawks for two years, despite being out of favour thorughout 2026.

The 20-year-old has kicked 39 goals from 31 games, but found himself behind Jack Gunston, Mitch Lewis and Mabior Chol. With Gunston signed on and Suns forward Ben King expected to sign with the Hawks as well, there were questions about whether Dear would get enough opportunity at his childhood club.

Hawks list boss Mark McKenzie said the club was "really pleased" that Dear had recommitted.

"He remains an important part of what we are trying to achieve as a club," he said.

"Following his debut season, Calsher showed us all the special talent that he is, but as a key tall at 21 years of age, we've needed to be patient with his progression.

"Having battled several injuries over his first three seasons in the system, we are very excited about what the future holds for Calsher with a strong pre-season under his belt and greater continuity into 2027 and beyond."

Thursday, Oct. 1
Goater set to make cross-city switch

North Melbourne defender Josh Goater is set to join the Hawks after requesting a trade on Thursday.

Having played just 18 games, the 23-year-old had fallen out of favour after an injury-hit run in his time at North.

Premiership Lion requests trade

The Brisbane Lions have confirmed Sam Marshall has requested a trade to St Kilda.

"The Brisbane Lions confirm premiership midfielder Sam Marshall has requested to be traded to St Kilda," the Lions said in a statement.

"Marshall has played 13 games, including the 2025 Premiership, across two seasons since being selected in the first round of the 2024 draft as a graduate of the Youi Brisbane Lions Academy.

"The club respects Marshall's request to be traded, and will work towards facilitating an outcome that best reflects true value to the Brisbane Lions for the 20-year-old."

Tuesday, Sept. 29
Neale informs Lions he intends to join Collingwood

Two-time Brownlow Medal winner Lachie Neale has told Brisbane he will depart the club as an unrestricted free agent and sign a three-year deal with Collingwood.

Aware that Neale intended to leave at the end of the year, the Lions never offered him a new contract.

The paperwork for the deal is expected to be formalised as early as Friday when the free agency period opens.

Friday, Sept. 25
Jordon Butts to join the Bulldogs

Zak Butters isn't the only South Australian-based player keen to join the Western Bulldogs, with Crows' key defender Jordon Butts officially naming the Dogs as his preferred offseason destination.

The unrestricted free agent will sign a five-year deal at the Kennel, according to AFL.com.au.

Tuesday, Sept. 22
Amartey officially names Carlton

Wantaway Sydney forward Joel Amartey has confirmed his desire to join Carlton as an unrestricted free agent.

The 26-year-old was kept out of the Swans' side with an Achilles injury in the latter stages of the year.

With Charlie Curnow (75 goals in 2026) and Logan McDonald (51) cementing their spots in the Sydney forward line as the prime targets, Amartey is hoping for more opportunity at the Blues.

Thursday, Sept. 17
GWS captain finally makes big call on his future

Toby Greene has opted to leave GWS, telling the AFL club he wishes to play with Geelong next season. Greene, who has been at the Giants since their foundation season in 2012, wants to go back to Victoria for family reasons.

In an extraordinary way to announce the decision, outgoing GWS boss Dave Matthews confirmed Greene's intentions on radio, before the club released a statement.

The 32-year-old has been offered a lucrative three-year deal to join the Cats.

Saturday, Sept. 12
Zak Butters makes huge free agency call
The year's hottest restricted free agent Zak Butters has made a huge call on his future, nominating the Western Bulldogs as his preferred destination.

After a year of speculation, with Geelong thought to be the front-runner for the Power star's signature, Butters made the call on Saturday, first reported by AFL.com.au's Callum Twomey.

The deal is reportedly for nine years.

Thursday, Sept. 10
Hogan set to join Pies
GWS and Collingwood have both confirmed that 2024 Coleman Medal winner Jesse Hogan has chosen the Magpies at his next home.

Set to be a four-club player, Hogan is 31 and coming off a 12-goal season from just nine appearances.

It's a big boost for the Magpies if Hogan can recapture his form; key forward has been an area of concern for a number of years.

Tuesday, Sept. 8
Bailey set to be Lion for life
Brisbane's Zac Bailey has ended months of 'will he, won't he' speculation to sign with the Lions for eight years, taking him through the 2034 season, the the club confirmed on Tuesday.

Bailey, a free agent, had been a big target for the Crows, who had reportedly tabled a more lucrative offer.

"I'm absolutely rapt to be staying at the Brisbane Lions," Bailey said in a statement.

"I love the environment here, the players, coaches and staff who all make it a great place to be and I feel like this Club continues to bring the best out of me.

"This Club means so much to me - I came here as a young player and have grown up here and to know I will be here long-term is something I'm really proud of.

"I would like to thank the club, my partner Em, my family and my management for being so supportive throughout this process.

"I love what we as a club have achieved during my time here and I am super excited about what we can continue to achieve together."

Rowan Marshall requests trade
St Kilda ruck Rowan Marshall looks set to be on the move, with the Saints confirming the big man had requested a trade for the second straight season.

While Marshall hasn't requested a specific club, it's likely to be Geelong after he failed to secure a trade to the Cats last year. He played 21 games for the Saints this seaosn, juggling ruck duties with Tom De Koning, who came in from Carlton last offseason.

"Rowan is a highly valued member of the St Kilda Football Club and remains contracted until the end of 2027," the Saints said in a statement.

"Marshall has not nominated a preferred destination at this stage, with the club making clear that any trade will need to be in the best interests of the St Kilda Football Club."

Zane Duursma wants to go to Melbourne
The No. 4 pick in the 2023 AFL draft Zane Duursma has requested a trade out of North Melbourne, with Melbourne in his sights.

The news comes a week after coach Alastair Clarkson was sacked by the club. North won nine games in 2026, their best return since 2019.

Ed Allan re-signs with the Pies
After speculation about his future at the Magpies, mdifielder Ed Allan has put pen to paper, signing a four year extension to remain at Collingwood.

2026 was a breakout season for Allan, who played 19 games and averaged a career-high 16.5 disposals per game.

Monday, Sept. 7
Pair of in-demand Dogs re-sign
According to afl.com.au, both Arty Jones and Buku Khamis will remain at the Kennel this offseason.

Jones will sign a three-year deal, while Khamis has a five-year contract in front of him.

Essendon and Brisbane had interest in livewire forward Jones, who had a standout performance against Collingwood in the wildcard final win, while the Blues were heavily linked to Khamis for a second straight offseason.

Cooper Hodge nomintes Hawthorn
A big boost for the Hawks, with club champion Luke Hodge's son Cooper choosing to join the Melbourne-based team as a father-son at this year's draft.

He had the option of going to Brisbane as a Lions academy member.

stories.headline: Christian Horner: Mercedes' Toto Wolff has it 'easy' at the moment
stories.summary: Former Red Bull team principal Christian Horner has suggested that Mercedes boss Toto Wolff has "got it quite easy" at the moment.
stories.body:
Former Red Bull team principal Christian Horner has suggested that Mercedes boss Toto Wolff has "got it quite easy" at the moment.

Horner, 52, officially left Red Bull Racing in September last year having been relieved of "operational duties" following last July's British Grand Prix. It ended a 20-year career with the team, where he won eight drivers' and six constructors' titles.

The past decade saw Horner spar with Wolff as Red Bull and Mercedes did battle.

This season, Horner's old team are currently fourth in the constructors' standings with 11 podiums and two wins, both claimed by Max Verstappen during this month's races in Bahrain and Singapore.

Mercedes top the constructors' leaderboard, while Kimi Antonelli is first in the drivers' standings having won eight races so far.

A potential return to F1 for Horner remains a hot topic and in an interview earlier this year, Wolff suggested Horner had "broken a lot of glass."

In an interview with the Guardian, Horner said: "He [Wolff] also said this [Red Bull] engine was going to be completely s--t and a disaster.

"Toto's got it quite easy at the moment. Zak Brown [head of McLaren] is compromised because he's using Toto's engine so he can't ruffle feathers.

"All sport needs rivalry, whether it's [Alex] Ferguson and [Arsene] Wenger, [Jose] Mourinho and (Pep) Guardiola. It percolates and polarises. I used that to galvanise good people to take on Mercedes."

- Formula 1 to return to Africa in 'early 2030s' as Rwanda race confirmed

- 'Chucky' Verstappen is back. Luckily for Antonelli and Mercedes, it's too late

- Toto Wolff finds quirky solution to Kimi Antonelli track limits 'stress'

Horner also revealed in the interview that he has suffered from panic attacks and has worked to recognise the symptoms.

"I didn't know what it was. You suddenly feel dizzy and conscious of your breathing and you think there's something strange going on. I put it down to having had too much coffee on an oppressive, muggy, thundery day," he said.

"Then it happened again. I got checked out and there was nothing physically the matter. They said: 'We think you have anxiety. Your breathing's very shallow.' It was my body telling me you're pushing pretty hard here. I'm able to recognise the symptoms now and let it go, and breathe."

stories.summary: Here's a look at every weight class to determine the best of the best in UFC, PFL and beyond.
stories.body:
Brendan Allen fought a back-and-forth battle with Christian Leroy Duncan in Saturday's UFC Fight Night main event. Going into the fifth round of the meeting of top-10 middleweights, Allen was narrowly ahead on all three scorecards. Of course, he did not know what the judges were thinking.

So Allen took it out of the judges' hands in Round 5, getting Duncan to the ground and efficiently finishing the gritty fight with a rear-naked choke.

With his fourth straight victory, Allen moves up one spot to No. 5 in the ESPN divisional rankings, continuing his recent climb in the middleweight top 10.

That's the only rankings change this week. Duncan remains No. 10 at 185 pounds, and sixth-ranked strawweight Loopy Godínez, who beat unranked Ketlen Souza by decision on Saturday's undercard, also retains her spot.

Here are the ESPN pound-for-pound MMA rankings and a list of current UFC champions in all weight classes.

Results are current; rankings as of Oct. 13. To be eligible for the rankings, a fighter must have competed over the past 12 months or must have an upcoming fight booked. Fighters who have been dropped for inactivity can be reinstated only after they compete.

stories.headline: St. Louis unbeaten run up to 20 games, tying Red Bulls' MLS record
stories.summary: Carlo Holse's hat trick helped St. Louis City SC beat the LA Galaxy 6-2 on Sunday night to extend their unbeaten streak across all competitions to 20 games.
stories.body:
ST. LOUIS -- Carlo Holse's hat trick in the first 21 minutes -- the second hat trick in club history -- helped St. Louis City beat the LA Galaxy 6-2 on Sunday night to extend their unbeaten streak across all competitions to 20 games and tie the MLS record.

St. Louis, which is 13-0-5 in its last 18 regular-season games, tied the mark set when the New York Red Bulls went unbeaten in an MLS-record 20 consecutive games across all competitions in 2016.

Rafael Navarro converted from the penalty spot in the 45th minute, scored again in the 53rd and added two assists for St. Louis (14-6-8). Lukas MacNaughton scored on a diving header in the seventh minute of first-half stoppage time and Roman Bürki had five saves.

Holse opened the scoring in the second minute, added a goal in the seventh and skipped a shot inside the right post from the center of the area to make it 3-0 in the 21st minute to record the second-fastest hat trick in MLS history. Hany Mukhtar scored three goals for Nashville in the first 16 minutes of 5-1 win over Chicago on July 17, 2021.

The Galaxy's Kyōgo Furuhashi went off due to an apparent hamstring injury and was replaced in the 10th minute by João Klauss, whose goal in the 71st minute capped the scoring. Klauss, a 29-year-old midfielder in his first season with the Galaxy, had St. Louis City's first hat trick in a 3-3 tie with the Galaxy on June 14, 2025.

Robert Taylor scored in the 31st minute for the Galaxy (9-11-9).

St. Louis beat the Galaxy 3-1 on July 22 at Dignity Health Sports Park and hosts the Vancouver Whitecaps on Wednesday in a Western Conference top-of-table clash.

The Galaxy, who are clinging to the last playoff spot in the West, play the Portland Timbers at Dignity Health Sports Park on Wednesday. The Timbers are three points behind the Galaxy for ninth place -- the final playoff spot.

Information from The Associated Press was used in this report.

stories.headline: New Zealand Rugby launches legal action against ARLC over 'Chiefs' name
stories.summary: The battle over the use of the "Chiefs" name is headed to the New Zealand High Court after New Zealand Rugby launched legal action against the Australian Rugby League Commission.
stories.body:
The battle over the use of the "Chiefs" name is headed to the New Zealand High Court after New Zealand Rugby launched legal action against the Australian Rugby League Commission.

NZR on Thursday said it had been left with no choice but to launch legal proceedings against the ARLC, who has sought to adopt the name for its Papua New Guinea expansion franchise.

The PNG Chiefs are due to join the NRL in 2028 and have already signed a raft of players, including code-hoppers Zac Lomaz and Joey Manu, but they may yet have to undergo a chanGe of name if NZR gets its way.

The Chiefs' Super Rugby franchise has existed since 1996, with NZR claiming the introduction of the PNG Chiefs would result in "significant confusion and damage" should they be allowed to compete under the name from 2028.

"New Zealand Rugby (NZR) has today moved to protect the Chiefs brand and is filing proceedings in the High Court of New Zealand against the decision by the Australian Rugby League Commission (ARLC) to launch a new NRL side using "Chiefs" in its name," an NZR statement read.  

"NZR is seeking both an interim and final injunction which stops the use of the names 'PNG Chiefs', 'Chiefs' or any other similar names in New Zealand.   

"The Chiefs have competed as a professional rugby team in Super Rugby since 1996 and over those 30 years, have built a strong identity and fanbase across New Zealand, Australia and internationally.  

"In New Zealand, NZR owns both the trademark rights for the word Chiefs and the Chiefs logo and since 1998, NZR has also held trademark protection for the Chiefs logo in Australia."

NZR claims it had tried to engage with the ARLC in an attempt to find a resolution, yet the commission was now intent on proceeding with the official launch of the PNG Chiefs on Oct. 21.

"For 30 years the Chiefs and their players have built an incredibly strong identity that is widely recognised and loved by fans," NZR chief executive Steve Lancaster said. "We have raised our concerns with the ARLC directly and consistently over the last year in attempting to find a resolution. We now have a responsibility to protect the Chiefs brand.   

"We want to be absolutely clear, this is not about rugby league's growth in the Pacific. We welcome the development of the Pacific region through sport and the passion that the people of Papua New Guinea have for both rugby and rugby league."  

The Chiefs won two Super Rugby titles in back-to-back seasons in 2012 and 2013, and were runners-up in Super Rugby Pacific this season after suffering a crushing defeat by the Hurricanes in the decider.

The Hamilton-based team has produced countless All Blacks since its inception, with Saturday's run-on team to face the Wallabies featuring six players from the franchise.

"Here in New Zealand, when people hear 'the Chiefs', they think of this club and this region. The identity carries significant cultural meaning and connection to the region and its people, we know it means a great deal to our players and coaches past and present, fans and supporters here and around the world," Chiefs CEO Simon Graafhuis said.   

"Teams in different sports and markets can exist alongside one another with the same name, but the issue here is the similarity of our sports competing in the same market, for the same fans, in overlapping windows."  

However, ARLC executive chairman Peter V'Landys later issued a stinging rebuke, insisting he would vigorously defend PNG's right to use the Chiefs as its team name.

"The hypocrisy is mind-blowing, considering the Auckland Blues in 1996 used the NSW Blues name without any consultation or approval. The NSW Blues had been the Blues for in excess of 50 years before that," he said.

"Rugby union is obviously feeling threatened by rugby league in New Zealand, with sell-outs at most rugby league games."

No date has yet been slated for the hearing in New Zealand's High Court.
